Team -

Novus (deal DLS-7349) reported a production outage-like symptom at ~10:32am ET: high latency, 429s, retries. Customer supplied traces and a payload sample (attached). My read: routing caused a subset of traffic to be served by a burst-limited pool; suspect "quota mapping" misalignment between their account and our regional policy (per-customer leaky-bucket vs per-route window).

Impact: customer-facing triage queue degraded, revenue risk during renewal. Need fast verification of: 1) whether any routing fallback or pool shrink occurred at 10:30 2) check token-bucket configs for their account + any recent policy changes pushed during deploys 3) confirm if any throttles were applied for duplicate API keys.

Attaching: rate-policy-config.yaml from the request (they included it). Please treat as P1 and post findings. If we confirm misconfiguration, we need an exec note to commit a temporary quota override and a post-mortem ask to patch the policy mapping logic.

--Marcus

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 12:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: INC: Novus Health - urgent throughput/429s (possible quota/policy mapping)

Quick update from infra: at 10:29:47 ET we triggered a regional routing recalculation for a small set of sessions after a transient NVMe anomaly on a host. Traffic for Novus's account (acct_id: nv-9923) was moved to a secondary pool that had an unintentionally tighter burst window (per-route burst_limit=800 tokens / 30s vs expected 2500/60s). That mapping was introduced in a deploy on 2026-11-28 intended for cost isolation.

Consequence: the pattern of parallel short-lived streams from Novus saturated the burst window, causing back-to-back 429s and queueing which manifested as higher P95 latency. I've applied a temporary override to align the pool's burst window to the expected settings for nv-9923 and removed the faulty mapping. The override expires in 4 hours while we validate.

Attached: request-trace-20261130.log excerpt and the policy diff.

Next steps I propose:
- Formal rollback of the 11/28 mapping by ops (schedule immediate patch)
- Admit a postmortem to analyze why mapping tests didn't catch this distribution (esp. per-customer traffic shapes)
- If legal/renewal asks, request an executive credit hold until PM provides remediation timeline

--Rishi
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
